one_month_reasoning: No Snowflake earnings fall in the window. Q2 FY27 was reported 2026-09-02, and Q3 FY27 has not been dated by the company; early December is likely (Q3 FY26 was reported 2025-12-03). Events in the window: (1) The $3.75B 0% converts close on Oct 1 ($2.0B 2029 notes convertible at $500.38 and $1.75B 2031 notes at $483.98), along with the ~$262M-face repurchase of the 2027 notes. Hedging pressure from convert arbitrage mostly happened at pricing, and the capped calls, capped at $820.30, add some bid while dealers set up their hedges, so I expect this to be neutral to slightly supportive. (2) A ruling on the motion to dismiss the third amended complaint in the older securities action could land in October, and the company's MTD in the newer consolidated action is due Oct 13 (a filing, not a ruling). Both are small for valuation. (3) Hyperscaler cloud results come in late October. (4) Macro: October FOMC hike odds fell to ~36% after the cooler Sep 30 PCE print, so there is two-sided rate risk for a long-duration name at ~16x sales. Post-earnings drift and the pullback from the $384.56 high roughly offset. I have no edge, so I use a lognormal centred at ~$338 with monthly vol of ~17.5% (62%/3.5).

fair_value.method: Blend of 12-month-forward EV/NTM sales (60%, ~$337 at 13.5x on ~$9.6B NTM revenue as of Sep 2027) and an NTM FCF multiple (40%, ~$313 at 50x on ~$2.4B adj. FCF). Both use ~$2.0B net cash as of Sep 2027 (pro forma ~$1.5B today) and ~390M diluted shares. At 13x the EV/sales leg would be ~$325.

methods.inputs: NTM revenue as of Sep 2027 ~$9.6B x 13.5x = $129.6B EV + ~$2.0B net cash = $131.6B / 390M shares = ~$337 (at 13x: ~$325; at 14x: ~$350)

About 1/3 of FY28 (~$8.2B) plus 2/3 of FY29 (~$10.3B at ~+25-27%). The supervisor's cross-check gives ~$9.5-9.8B.

Cut from 14x. The supervisor notes that 14x is the top of the 8-15x high-growth band and assumes ~30% growth persists, while the peer line for mid/high-20s growth centres ~13x. I stay slightly above 13x because the alt data still points to share gain overall (PredictLeads net inflow ~4:1 overall, ~2:1 vs close competitors) and FCF margins are ~25%. I do not go higher because Databricks' own disclosure (>$7B run-rate, >80%) shows its Lakehouse/DBSQL warehouse business at >$1.5B growing >100%, which competes head-on with Snowflake's core. The April 2026 trough was 7-9x (TIKR/Substack) and the sector median is 3.6x (Clouded Judgement).

Jul-31 cash plus investments of $4.33B, plus ~$3.70B net convert proceeds, minus $383.5M capped calls and $548.3M to repurchase ~$261.8M face of the 2027 notes (in the money, converting at $157.50), against ~$5.8B face debt: ~$1.5B pro forma today. Add ~$1.6B of 12-month adj. FCF minus ~$0.65B/yr of RSU tax withholding and ~$0.4B of buybacks: ~$2.0B. Round 1 had $1.8B today, which was too high.

Q3 non-GAAP diluted guide of 382M, plus ~2% net SBC dilution. The ~5M excess shares from the 2024 notes above the $225 capped-call cap are roughly covered because the old notes are counted as debt at face. The new notes are not dilutive below $484-500, and the capped calls cover them up to $820.30.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: NTM adj. FCF as of Sep 2027 ~$2.4B (25% margin on $9.6B) x 50x = $120B + ~$2.0B net cash / 390M = ~$313

inputs_detail.derivation: Guidance of 23%, plus operating leverage: the non-GAAP operating margin guide was raised to 14.5%, and job-posting data (Revelio) show GTM hiring cut while engineering hiring is focused on AI.

A high multiple for ~27-30% growth. It stays at 50x rather than higher because GAAP SBC is ~27% of revenue (Q2 $423.6M on $1.55B, per the supervisor from 10-Q Note 12), so owner FCF net of SBC is close to zero. The method is a cross-check that discounts for SBC against the sales multiple.

bear.story: The AI consumption step-up proves one-off, and Databricks (>$7B run-rate, >80%; warehouse product >$1.5B, >100%) takes the incremental warehouse and AI workloads. The PredictLeads net-migration ratio against close competitors turns negative. Product growth falls to the low-20s in the FY28 guide, and the multiple de-rates toward ~8-9x NTM sales as in April 2026. SBC at ~27% of revenue keeps the stock from looking cheap.

base.story: Growth fades gradually from 37% to the high-20s (FY28 ~+29%), and FCF margin reaches ~25%. The multiple compresses from ~16-17x to ~13-13.5x NTM sales, which roughly offsets revenue growth, so the stock ends near today's level and near my $328 fair value.

bull.story: Cortex/Snowflake Intelligence keep growth at 33-35%+ into FY28, NRR rises, and alt-data inflows persist even as Databricks grows. The market pays ~18x for a durable AI data platform, and the stock reaches the ~$484-500 convert conversion prices (the capped calls, capped at $820, absorb dilution above that).

thesis_break_reason: Around $215, ~36% below today and near the early-summer breakout level, the market would be pricing a real deceleration (product growth back under ~25%, NRR rolling over, or a weak FY28 guide), not ordinary volatility. At 13x, $215 implies NTM revenue of only ~$6.3B, which is roughly today's run-rate. The alt-data checks for this are the PredictLeads detection/migration ratio against close competitors turning negative, and Databricks' warehouse (Lakehouse/DBSQL) run-rate keeping >100% growth past ~$2.5B, which would mean it is taking Snowflake's core workload.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor's checks, which I verified where cheap, moved three inputs. (1) Net cash: the 2027 notes convert at $157.50 and are deep in the money, so the $548.3M repurchase retires only ~$261.8M of face (confirmed in the company pricing release). With capped calls of $383.5M, pro forma net cash is ~$1.5B today and ~$2.0B by Sep 2027, versus my $1.8B, a small effect (~-$1/share at Sep 2027). (2) Multiple: I agree that 14x is the top of the band for growth fading into the high-20s. I move to 13.5x rather than the supervisor's 13x because my lane's evidence (PredictLeads net inflows, new detections +72%, GTM hiring cuts that help margins) still leans modestly positive. That changes the EV/sales leg from $355 to $337. (3) Databricks: I confirmed the company's own Aug 13, 2026 release (>$7B run-rate, >80%, plus a $5B raise at $190B), which I now treat as one original source rather than CNBC plus Tunguz. The same release says its Lakehouse warehouse product is >$1.5B and growing >100%, which is direct competition for Snowflake's core and argues against paying a higher multiple. The supervisor was asked how the migration ratio would change if Databricks keeps growing >80%. PredictLeads already shows Databricks taking 54% of Snowflake's departures while Snowflake is net-gaining overall. That can hold because the market is growing and Snowflake is winning from legacy/other vendors. The vendor data is unverified, though, so I weight it lightly and treat a flip in the head-to-head ratio as a thesis-break signal rather than a base-case input. I dropped WallStreetBets sentiment and the anonymous bull-case Substack as evidence, per the source review. The FCF leg stays at $313 (50x; GAAP SBC is ~27% of revenue, not higher). The blended fair value falls from $340 to $328, about 3% below spot. The ladder is a lognormal with median ~$335 (was ~$345) and sigma ~0.55, a fattened left tail for de-rating risk, and a right tail kept (P>=844 3.5%, which the supervisor found fine given the $118-385 move). Scenario mean is ~$341. The 1-month ladder is roughly symmetric at 17.5% monthly vol, centred ~$338: there are no earnings in the window, and the convert close, the possible MTD ruling, the FOMC and hyperscaler prints are two-sided. Research this round was limited to two verification searches.
